title: Maintenance
text:
Local repository connections · Native Git commands
Each course contains ordinary local template files. The repositories are independent: a normal clone contains the files needed by that course. There is no custom template manager, _teaching/ directory, lock manifest, Git subtree or Git submodule in the current setup.
Use feature commits to transfer improvements. A feature commit contains only the reusable change and all files required to implement it. Git fetch reads another repository’s commits; cherry-pick applies one selected commit to the current branch. It creates a new commit, rather than continuously linking files.










Repository
Remote
Destination




Outils informatique II
origin
Its existing https://github.com/e5k/outils-info-2.git repository


Outils informatique II
template
Local _quarto-course-template repository


Analyse géospatiale
template
Local _quarto-course-template repository


Central template
outils-info-2
Local Outils informatique II repository


Central template
analyse-geospatiale
Local Analyse géospatiale repository



All three use main. The initial setup used local paths. The central template is now public at e5k/quarto-teaching-template. Its origin points to that GitHub repository, and the two courses’ template remotes now use the same URL. The template’s course-source remotes remain local paths; update those separately when the source course has a published repository. Analyse géospatiale has not been published by this setup.
Check the repository you are about to edit:
git status --short
git branch --show-current
git remote -v
The setup committed the 53 shared files after checking they matched byte for byte across the three folders. It preserved existing file contents and unrelated edits. Analyse géospatiale initially tracks only the shared files; its chapters, local YAML, bibliography and planning files still need deliberate source commits. Do not mistake its template baseline for a complete course backup.
The tag teaching-template-baseline-2026-11-04 refers to the template’s initial commit, 12493da. The courses have their own shared-file baseline commits (cb054d0 for Outils informatique II and abb5bcc for Analyse géospatiale). These are setup snapshots, not feature commits to import.



Make a change in the template or a course. Stage exact paths, then inspect the staged diff:
# Example: a change to the profile-icons feature
git add -- slides/_template.yml slides/_extensions/course/author-links/
git diff --cached
git commit -m "Template: improve author profile icons"
git rev-parse HEAD
Use the paths appropriate to the actual feature. If a file contains both shared and course-specific changes, git add -p -- path/to/file lets you stage selected hunks. Check git diff --cached for all staged content: git commit without path arguments includes everything staged, including any earlier work.
Do not include course titles, chapter edits, bibliography entries, datasets or personal URLs in the shared feature commit. Commit those separately in the course repository. New plugins typically need a YAML declaration and a complete extension directory; adding only a configuration line leaves an incomplete feature.



Run in the destination course:
git fetch template
git log --oneline teaching-template-baseline-2026-11-04..template/main
git show TEMPLATE_COMMIT
git cherry-pick -x TEMPLATE_COMMIT
Replace TEMPLATE_COMMIT with a real feature hash from the log. git show displays the whole commit, not just one file; review it before applying. The baseline range omits the initial template commit but does not guarantee every later commit is shareable. Documentation and starter-content commits must also be reviewed for relevance.
-x records the source hash in the new commit message. If a feature spans several commits, inspect and import each in dependency order. Do not cherry-pick a whole branch or broad range just to obtain one feature.



First commit the reusable feature in the source course. Then run in the central template:
git fetch outils-info-2
git log --oneline outils-info-2/main
git show COURSE_COMMIT
git cherry-pick -x COURSE_COMMIT
git rev-parse HEAD
Use analyse-geospatiale in place of outils-info-2 for that source. Take the new template hash printed by the final command and import it into the other course with the template-to-course procedure.
The source course already has the feature; do not send the same change back to it. Cherry-picked copies have different hashes, so hash inequality alone does not prove a feature is missing. Read the -x provenance and inspect the content. Keep the template commit message clear enough to recognise the feature later.
Do not git pull or merge an entire course branch into the template: the branch also contains local lessons and configuration. These independent repositories do not have a shared course-history model.



After creating a new course repository and committing its matching shared files, connect it locally:
# In the course; replace the path for your computer
git remote add template /path/to/_quarto-course-template
git fetch template

# In the template; replace both placeholders
git remote add my-course /path/to/my-course
git fetch my-course
For GitHub-backed collaboration, create each repository and push its own branch intentionally. Then change the template and course-source URLs to those verified repository URLs with git remote set-url. Merely changing a URL does not create the remote repository or publish any files. Keep each course’s own origin distinct from its template remote. Avoid inventing or copying an unverified URL.

title: Maintenance
text:
2 Local changes and conflicts
Prefer a clean working tree before importing a feature. Commit unrelated course work on its own first. If you need to set it aside temporarily:
git stash push -u -m "Before template update"
git fetch template
git cherry-pick -x TEMPLATE_COMMIT
git stash pop
-u includes untracked files, but not ignored files. Inspect what is untracked before stashing: an untracked planning dataset may be large. A stash is local storage, not a remote backup. Restoring it can produce a second set of conflicts even after the cherry-pick succeeds.
If Git pauses a cherry-pick:
git status
# Edit each conflicting file and remove conflict markers.
git add -- path/to/resolved-file
git cherry-pick --continue
To abandon the in-progress import, use git cherry-pick --abort. To undo a completed, published import, consider a new git revert commit after inspecting its scope; do not rewrite shared history casually. An empty cherry-pick often means the feature is already present—inspect before choosing git cherry-pick --skip.
Git does not understand which YAML values are “generic”. The YAML split and focused commits provide that boundary. If a conflict mixes a course bibliography path with a shared plugin setting, keep the path local and move the plugin change into the appropriate _template.yml.

title: Maintenance
text:
5 Verify an update
After an import, review git show --stat HEAD and the changed lines. Validate the outputs affected by the feature:







Change
Useful verification




Profiles or callouts
Render the same chapter under both profiles; inspect written answers, code output, numbering and collapsed answers.


Exercises
Try a correct, incorrect and blank response; check grouping and solution toggles.


Notebook conversion
Open the resulting notebook; confirm code cells, outputs, Markdown wrappers and answer-source policy.


Slide layout or animation
Present a representative deck, step through every affected fragment and inspect different image heights.


Bibliography or portability
Refresh the copy, render citations, then copy slides/ elsewhere and preview it there.


PDF export
Run the normal Decktape workflow and inspect pages, including fragment captures.


Documentation
From doc/, run quarto render; verify links, search, examples and narrow-screen layout.



A successful --no-execute render checks the available layout and source processing; it does not validate analytical code. A successful browser demonstration does not establish PDF compatibility.

title: Maintenance
text:
6 Troubleshooting







Symptom
Check and correction




Specified Reveal plugin directory 'animate' does not exist
Confirm you copied slides/_extensions/fradav/animate/ and are using the slide project’s YAML. The whole directory is needed.


Deck renders as an ordinary HTML page
Check that its filename matches slides/_quarto.yml → project.render; then confirm the separate slide project is loaded.


clean-revealjs is not found
Restore slides/_extensions/grantmcdermott/clean/ and its manifest.


Question blocks look like ordinary text
Source must use .question / .answer; load the custom-callout filter and definitions.


Missing question number or duplicate header
Use exr- / sol- IDs; keep the header integration script and CSS together. Matching suffixes pair answers with questions.


Answers appear in a question render
Inspect document answers overrides and confirm every written answer is wrapped conditionally.


Code runs although its answer is hidden
Conditional visibility does not disable execution. Review cell eval options.


Notebook still contains answers
Expected with the current converter; it retains source and does not apply profile filtering.


Number 01 notebook will not build
The current discovery code always excludes 01. Change it deliberately for a course with a first-class practical.


Nothing rendered for a slide selector
The script only warns on missing slide names. Check the actual files and use a matching selector.


Missing references in an extracted deck
Run the slide script before extraction; check slides/assets/ and the local bibliography path.


Profile icons absent
Supply at least one valid HTTP(S) author-links URL; check first-author markup, filter registration and the icon stylesheet.


SVG animation fails from a local file
Serve the deck over HTTP; verify SVG paths, IDs, the filter and plugin.


Lightbox does not open
.lightbox is a marker; enable lightbox: true locally as well.


Layout overflows after an image offset
Relative offsets do not alter reserved layout space. Reduce media size or use normal columns before offsets.


decktape or gs cannot be found
Install the required tool or use --no-pdf; use --no-compress when only Ghostscript is missing.


Unexpected template content imported
Inspect the chosen commit. Cherry-pick copies the entire commit; use focused feature commits and abort unresolved imports if needed.

title: Maintenance
text:
7 Maintain this manual
The documentation is an independent Quarto website under doc/ in the template repository. Its render list names exactly four guide pages and the index. The manual loads a local copy of the course’s shared _template.yml, including its actual assets/custom.css and assets/dark.scss, profile files, notebook-link filter, CSL and after-body scripts. Supporting assets also include the custom-callout extension and exercise files required by live examples. These are local snapshots: refresh the shared YAML and its companion files together when the source theme changes. Keep assets/docs.css limited to documentation layout so that it does not replace the course palette or typography. Directory-level _metadata.yml keeps the documentation language and table-of-contents label in English and disables external comments after the shared project metadata has been loaded.
The embedded slide deck is a pre-rendered demonstration made with the real slide project. Rebuild it when the slide theme changes, keeping the HTML and its dependency directory together under doc/assets/demos/slides/. Its downloadable source is supplied there as demo.qmd.txt to preserve the five-page QMD structure. To rebuild, copy that source into an isolated copy of the template’s slide project, rename it demo.qmd, include demo.qmd in that copy’s project.render list, add the supplied SVG, then render with Quarto. The documentation’s ordinary render does not rebuild the embedded deck.

title: Maintenance
text:
8 Documentation publication
The public website is https://e5k.github.io/quarto-teaching-template/. Sources live on main; only doc/ is rendered by .github/workflows/publish-docs.yml. A push affecting doc/** or that workflow starts a build with Quarto 1.8.27. The action updates gh-pages and explicitly deploys the rendered doc/_site/ artifact using GitHub Pages. It can also be run manually from the repository’s Actions tab.
GitHub Pages uses the GitHub Actions publishing method. The gh-pages branch is maintained as the rendered publication output; doc/_site/ stays ignored on main. The course starter book at the repository root is not published as this website.
For a manual local publication, run quarto render doc followed by quarto publish gh-pages doc --no-render --no-browser from the repository root. The automated workflow is preferred for regular updates because it also performs the explicit Pages deployment.

title: Book guide
text:
Native profiles · Local settings
The book is one project with two mutually exclusive profiles, answer and question. The profile group is declared in root _template.yml; profile values live in _quarto-answer.yml and _quarto-question.yml.








Setting
Answer profile
Question profile




answers
true

execute.echo
true

execute.output
true

Written answer content
Visible when wrapped with when-meta="answers"
Removed from rendered output by the same condition


Notebook and other links
Displayed; .ipynb links receive download
Entire .quarto-other-links region hidden by CSS



quarto render --profile answer
quarto render --profile question
Root _template.yml defaults to answers: true. Both builds normally use the same _book/ directory, so the most recent render replaces the corresponding output. Archive or copy a completed build if you need to retain both variants.


Wrap every written answer that should disappear from the question version:
::: {.content-visible when-meta="answers"}
The pattern supports an association, but does not establish causation.
:::
Hiding output does not hide ordinary Markdown or Python source. Conditional content also does not prevent execution of wrapped cells. For a specific cell, use native execution options deliberately:
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: true
print("A displayed result without the source code")
```
echo controls source display, output controls results and eval controls whether the cell runs. An explicit cell option can override project defaults. Do not use visibility rules as a substitute for execution control.



A chapter containing the following metadata can behave differently from its selected profile:
answers: true
execute:
  output: false
This combination is present in some existing course material: written answers can remain visible while cell results stay hidden. Remove overrides when you want profile values to govern the page. Render the actual chapter under both profiles and inspect the result; do not infer visibility only from the command name.

title: Book guide
text:
2 Questions and answers
Extension: custom-callout · Native cross-references · Local header integration
The custom-callout extension reads the definitions in _template.yml. Use .question or .answer in the source. The extension converts these into rendered .callout-question and .callout-answer elements. Writing .callout-question directly bypasses this class-to-definition conversion.



Type
Configured label
Icon
Colour
Default collapse




.question
Question
fa-circle-question
#6f42c1
No


.answer
Réponse
fa-circle-check
#2e8b57
Yes in HTML




2.1 Number a question and its answer
::: {#exr-compare .question title="Compare the two distributions"}
Which feature changes when the extreme value is removed?
:::

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="answers"}
::: {#sol-compare .answer title="Réponse"}
Return to @exr-compare.

The median changes less than the mean.
:::
::::
exr- activates native exercise numbering. sol- activates a solution; the matching suffix compare lets the local header script associate the answer with the question. IDs must be unique throughout the book. Use stable descriptive IDs so links survive title edits. Put the whole answer, including its title and source cells, inside the conditional wrapper. The outer wrapper uses four colons to make nesting clear.
Rendered example, with answers visible in this manual:

Question 1  





QuestionCompare the two distributions



Which summary is usually less sensitive to one extreme value: the mean or the median?



Solution 1. 





AnswerRéponse





The median is usually less sensitive. Return to question 1.





2.2 Titles and header numbering
Supply title="..." on the source div, or use a first heading inside it. If both are present, the title attribute wins. The extension also accepts icon, appearance and collapse div attributes; the global settings supply defaults.
The local assets/theme-toggle.html script finds native question/solution labels and moves them into the coloured header. An answer with the matching suffix receives the corresponding question number, with “Question” replaced by “Réponse”. It removes a redundant answer title when that title is simply “Réponse” or “Answer”. Root assets/custom.css suppresses the original separate numbering line.
Transfer all three layers together: the custom-callout extension, the custom-callout definitions in _template.yml, and the CSS/JS header integration. A styled block without an exr- ID is a callout, but is not a numbered exercise.
The book’s custom types are not configured in slides/_template.yml. To use them in slides, you would need to add their extension and definitions to the slide project; ordinary Quarto callouts already work there.

title: Book guide
Book guide
text:
4 Notebook links and conversion
Local Lua filter and Python builder
Add the download link in a chapter’s YAML:
other-links:
  - text: Notebook Jupyter
    icon: file-earmark-code
    href: class_02.ipynb
The notebook sits beside its source chapter, so the link is relative to that page. The Lua filter scripts/notebook-links.lua inspects the effective answers metadata:

When it is true, JavaScript adds download to links in .quarto-other-links whose href ends exactly with .ipynb.
Otherwise, CSS hides all .quarto-other-links, including any unrelated links placed there. Links elsewhere in the page are unaffected.

The filter does not generate notebooks or prevent someone opening a known notebook URL. A query suffix such as .ipynb?download=1 does not match its current end-of-string selector.
python scripts/render_notebooks.py 2
python scripts/render_notebooks.py course/class_02.qmd
The script runs quarto convert, writes an IPYNB next to each chapter, then clears outputs, execution counts and cell metadata. It sets a generic Python 3 kernelspec. It removes #| cell-option lines, selected Quarto div wrappers, heading attributes, image attributes, pagebreak shortcodes and Font Awesome shortcodes.
Answer source remains in converted notebooks. The script does not evaluate when-meta="answers" or apply the question profile. It strips wrappers while retaining their content. Its wrapper-cleaning expression recognises exactly three-colon fences; longer nested fences can remain. Inspect a representative notebook before distribution, particularly chapters with nested answers and HTML exercises.
The book’s resources list must include course/*.ipynb if the generated notebooks should be copied into the published output. keep-ipynb: false concerns Quarto’s execution intermediates; it is separate from notebooks deliberately generated by this script.

title: Book guide
text:
5 Citations and references
Native Pandoc citations · Local Zotero convention
Keep each course’s Zotero export in root assets/. Choose its own filename: OI2.bib, geospatial.bib or another appropriate name. Set that path in root _quarto.yml; the shared _template.yml sets the CSL to assets/bulletin-of-volcanology.csl.
The interpretation follows previous work [@yourCitationKey].

@yourCitationKey provides the original method.

## References

::: {#refs}
:::
Use a real key from the bibliography. The #refs container chooses where references appear. A whole-book references appendix can be listed in book.appendices; the filename and chapter organisation belong to the course.
Do not manually edit Zotero-synchronised entries. Import new references into Zotero and refresh its export. The slide script copies root bibliography files into slides/assets/; see standalone slides.

title: Book guide
text:
6 Appearance and authoring helpers
Local CSS and JavaScript · Native HTML theming
The book uses Cosmo in light mode and Darkly plus assets/dark.scss in dark mode. Syntax highlighting is atom-one / dracula. Root assets/custom.css sets Source Sans Pro for text and Roboto Slab for headings, loaded from Google Fonts with local fallback fonts.








Helper or behaviour
Usage
Effect




.bg
[key phrase]{.bg}
Teal translucent marker effect, including wrapped lines. It is orange in slides.


.btn .btn-download
Apply to a Markdown link
Rounded orange-outline button; the download attribute is separate.


.nowrap-first-col
Apply to a table or wrapping div
Prevents wrapping in the first table column. Long content can overflow a narrow screen.


.reveal-embed
Apply to an iframe
Full-width 16:9 embedded deck; 4:3 on narrow screens.


Documentation icon links
A link containing .fa-book or .fa-graduation-cap
Compact raised icon beside a function name; not applied inside sup.


Table stripes
Automatic on table.table rows
Alternates odd rows using light/dark CSS variables.


Figure alignment
Automatic
Left-aligns ordinary Quarto figure images.



Live book highlight: a shared scientific question.
[Download data](data/samples.csv){.btn .btn-download download="samples.csv"}
The CSS styles the link; it does not provide the file. To add a Font Awesome icon, enable the bundled fontawesome shortcode extension in that page or project’s filters, then use:
[{{< fa download >}} Download data](data/samples.csv){.btn .btn-download}
The root starter’s shared filter list contains notebook-links.lua and custom-callout; it does not enable fontawesome globally. The installed extension folder alone does not activate its shortcode.

6.1 Code annotations and figures
Line numbers and hover annotations are enabled in the HTML book. Use native <1> comments and an immediately following annotation list. The local CSS moves the copy button away from annotations.
```{python}
values = [2, 4, 8]  # <1>
mean = sum(values) / len(values)  # <2>
```

1. The observations used in the calculation.
2. The arithmetic mean.
For Matplotlib figures, load the supplied style explicitly; copying the file does not activate it:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.style.use("assets/plots.mplstyle")
With Quarto’s normal document-relative execution, use ../assets/plots.mplstyle from a chapter in course/. If the course sets a project execution directory, adjust the path accordingly. The style sets Roboto, teal labels and a #fafafa figure background; it does not automatically switch plot colours in book dark mode.


6.2 Navigation and small fixes
The template enables section numbering, page navigation, book search and a right-hand table of contents to depth 4. Sidebar chapter numbers are hidden visually; this does not disable section numbering elsewhere. assets/book-index-link.html turns the first sidebar part label into a home link when the book uses the matching first-part structure; it does nothing when that element is absent.
assets/theme-toggle.html also wraps Quarto’s colour toggle to restore the scroll position after a theme switch. The same file currently contains the question/answer header integration, so keep it when transferring either feature. Hypothesis comments are enabled under comments.hypothesis in shared YAML and depend on the external service.
For native behaviour beyond the local configuration, consult conditional content, code annotations and citations.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
Create a course, write teaching materials and share improvements across courses using the same self-contained Quarto template.
This manual documents the template derived from Outils informatique II and used by Analyse géospatiale. It covers the HTML book, the customised clean-revealjs slide theme, the local teaching features and the Git workflow connecting them. Start with the first guide for a new course; use the other three as references while authoring.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
Getting started
Create a course, separate local and reusable YAML, prepare dependencies, name files, preview and build.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
Book guide
Use answer/question profiles, numbered callouts, exercises, notebooks, citations and light/dark styling.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
Slide guide
Compose layouts and fragments, animate figures, style text, configure profile icons and extract standalone slides.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
Maintenance
Move reusable commits between repositories, transfer complete dependencies and diagnose rendering problems.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
What belongs to the template
The template has two main content folders, course/ and slides/. Shared functionality is kept in _template.yml, local styles, filters, scripts and extension folders. Each course keeps its title, chapters, bibliography names and author details in its own _quarto.yml files.
The slide folder is also a Quarto project. It contains local dependencies so that you can copy the whole folder and present independently of the course book.

title: Quarto teaching template
section: The documentation uses the course theme
text:
The documentation uses the course theme
This website loads the same _template.yml as the course book, with local copies of assets/custom.css, assets/dark.scss and the accompanying scripts and filters. It therefore uses Source Sans Pro and Roboto Slab, the teal/orange palette, the customised light/dark appearance, table styling and code highlighting described in the book guide. assets/docs.css adds only the guide grid and other documentation layout rules. The local YAML keeps the documentation in English and disables external comments.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
Reading the feature descriptions
Each feature identifies its origin:







Label
Meaning




Native
Quarto, Pandoc or Reveal.js functionality, configured for this template.


Extension
Functionality supplied by a named third-party extension.


Local
A helper, configuration or modification present in this teaching setup. This label does not claim original authorship of upstream code.



The guides focus on the configured behaviour, including local differences. For example, .bg means a teal highlight in the book and an orange highlight in slides. Questions use the source class .question, not .callout-question; the latter is generated by the custom-callout extension.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
Scope of this draft
The reference was checked against the central template on 4 November 2026, using Quarto 1.8.27. Extension versions are recorded in Maintenance. A working slide demonstration is embedded in the slide guide; the book guide contains working callout and exercise examples. Examples referencing assets/example.png, a bibliography key or a dataset require your own corresponding resource.
HTML is the main teaching output. The Python scripts can also produce clean notebooks and slide PDFs, but those outputs do not reproduce every browser interaction. Compatibility notes are included where this distinction affects authoring.

title: Quarto teaching template
text:
Preview this manual
From this documentation folder:
quarto preview
Build the static website with quarto render. The five QMD pages render into _site/; this project has its own configuration and does not build the course book. Python execution is disabled for the manual, so example code is displayed without running analyses.
For the underlying platform, see the Quarto project guide and Reveal.js authoring guide.

title: Getting started
text:
Local
Copy the source files from _quarto-course-template into the new course directory. Include hidden source files such as .gitignore, but exclude the template’s .git/ directory, generated _book/, .quarto/ and presentation output folders. Initialise a new Git repository if the course does not already have one. Copying Git history is different from copying a course starter: do not accidentally give the course the template’s remotes.
The central template currently lives at:
/Users/seb/Documents/WORK/Teaching/_quarto-teaching-template
The normal source structure is:
my-course/
├── _quarto.yml
├── _template.yml
├── _quarto-answer.yml
├── _quarto-question.yml
├── index.qmd
├── assets/
│   ├── references.bib
│   ├── bulletin-of-volcanology.csl
│   ├── custom.css
│   ├── dark.scss
│   └── ...
├── _extensions/
├── scripts/
├── course/
│   └── class_01.qmd
└── slides/
    ├── _quarto.yml
    ├── _template.yml
    ├── _extensions/
    ├── assets/
    │   └── references.bib
    ├── mathjax-config.js
    └── slides_class_01.qmd
assets/references.bib is the starter’s example name. Choose a filename appropriate to the course and configure both projects to use it. Add data/, img/, appendices or other content directories when needed; they are not automatically shared template files.


Edit root _quarto.yml. Preserve the metadata-files reference and the book project type:
metadata-files:
  - _template.yml
project:
  type: book
  output-dir: _book
  resources:
    - course/*.ipynb
    - slides/*.html
    - slides/*.pdf
    - slides/*_files/**
    - slides/mathjax-config.js
book:
  title: My course
  author: My name
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - course/class_01.qmd
    - course/class_02.qmd
bibliography: assets/my-course.bib
jupyter: python3
keep-ipynb: false
Create each listed chapter before rendering the whole book. The resource patterns copy generated notebooks and presentation files into the book output; they do not generate those files. The build scripts produce them first.



Edit slides/_quarto.yml separately:
metadata-files:
  - _template.yml
project:
  type: default
  render:
    - slides_class_*.qmd
author:
  - name: My name
bibliography: assets/my-course.bib
The explicit project: type: default makes slides/ a separate project. Keep the project.render pattern consistent with the filenames you create: a deck outside that list may render without the project metadata, using plain HTML instead of clean-revealjs. The bibliography path resolves inside this project, to slides/assets/my-course.bib; it does not refer to the book’s root assets/ folder.

title: Getting started
text:
2 Understand the YAML split
Native composition · Local organisation








File
Contains
Keep out




Root _quarto.yml
Book title, author, chapters, bibliography, resource patterns, kernel, local publishing details
Reusable feature implementation


Root _template.yml
Book styles, filters, custom callout definitions, navigation defaults and profile group
A particular course’s title, chapter list or bibliography filename


slides/_quarto.yml
Author, profile URLs, bibliography, deck selection and local options
Changes intended for every course


slides/_template.yml
clean-revealjs, plugins, shared slide behaviour and CSL
Personal links, local bibliography filenames


A document’s YAML
Document title and deliberate page-specific overrides
Settings copied everywhere without a reason



Both projects load _template.yml through metadata-files. Change reusable behaviour there and local values in _quarto.yml. For complex settings such as filters and resource lists, inspect the resolved behaviour after editing: do not assume adding one local list item disables all inherited items.
Profiles add configuration for a selected build. Document metadata can override project or profile values. In particular, a chapter with answers: true can keep answers visible even when you request the question profile. See the profile checks.

title: Getting started
text:
3 Install the dependencies you need







Task
Requirements




Render Markdown-only book chapters and slides
Quarto; the bundled extension folders and local assets


Execute Python cells
The course’s Python environment, a Jupyter kernel matching jupyter, and imported packages


Run portable build scripts
Python 3.10 or later for the current script syntax; Quarto available on PATH


Generate slide PDFs
Decktape and its browser dependencies available on PATH


Compress slide PDFs
Ghostscript, exposed as gs


Interactive Python exercises used by Outils informatique II
pywebexercises, plus HTML output and the supplied webex CSS/JS


Transfer feature commits
Git and the configured repository remotes



Check the active tools before building:
quarto --version
quarto check jupyter
python --version
Activate the course environment first. The build scripts prepend their Python executable’s directory to the PATH used for rendering, which helps Quarto find the corresponding environment. This does not install packages or create a missing kernel.
The current theme declarations require at least Quarto 1.5.0 because of the custom-callout extension; use the tested 1.8.27 environment for this draft rather than treating that declared minimum as a tested compatibility guarantee.
The template uses Google Fonts, a Font Awesome CDN stylesheet for slides and a MathJax CDN script. A self-contained repository means the required source files live locally; it does not guarantee fully offline typography, icons, mathematics or access to external scientific services.

title: Getting started
text:
4 Name the files








Material
New naming
Existing supported naming




Chapter
course/class_02.qmd
course/semaine_02.qmd


Presentation
slides/slides_class_02.qmd
slides/slides_semaine_02.qmd


Notebook output
course/class_02.ipynb
course/semaine_02.ipynb



Use two digits and the same number across the three materials. Keep source filenames simple; displayed titles can contain accents and spaces. Avoid keeping both class_02.qmd and semaine_02.qmd for the same class: a numeric selector matches both.
The notebook script only discovers chapter filenames matching class_XX.qmd or semaine_XX.qmd. It always excludes number 01, even if you explicitly select it. This matches the current first class without a practical; adjust the script if another course needs a first-class notebook.

title: Getting started
text:
5 Preview and render directly
From the course root:
quarto preview
quarto render --profile answer
quarto render --profile question
quarto render course/class_02.qmd --profile answer
For slides, either render a named file from the root or work inside slides/:
quarto render slides/slides_class_02.qmd
cd slides
quarto preview
A direct slide render or preview does not refresh bibliography copies. Use the slide script after a Zotero update. --no-execute on a direct Quarto command skips code execution; it is useful for layout checks but cannot validate analytical results.

title: Getting started
text:
6 Use the portable build scripts
Local
Run these from the course root with the appropriate environment active:
# One slide deck as HTML only; also refreshes bibliography copies
python scripts/render_slides.py 2 --no-pdf

# One clean, unexecuted notebook
python scripts/render_notebooks.py 2

# All slides, then notebooks, then the book
python scripts/render_all.py --no-pdf








Script
Selection
Behaviour and options




render_slides.py
No selector: every slides/*.qmd; otherwise numbers, stems or filenames
Refreshes all root assets/*.bib copies first; runs Quarto for selected decks; PDF export and compression default to on. --no-pdf skips both; --no-compress keeps PDF export but skips Ghostscript.


render_notebooks.py
No selector: every discovered numbered chapter except 01
Converts QMD to IPYNB, removes outputs and execution state, strips selected Quarto markup. Missing selectors stop with an error.


render_all.py
Selectors narrow the slide and notebook steps
Always renders the whole book last. Forwards options to the slide script; it does not accept arbitrary Quarto flags. Then asks whether to publish.



Slide selectors that do not match a file only print a “Skipping missing presentation(s)” message. An empty selection can therefore finish without rendering anything; check the filenames and output rather than relying only on the exit code.
The combined script does not pass --profile question to the book render. Use a separate quarto render --profile question command for that build. --no-execute is a Quarto option, not a recognised script option; use the direct Quarto command when you need it.
After a successful combined build, the publication prompt accepts y, yes, o or oui and runs quarto publish gh-pages --no-render. Empty input or end-of-input skips publication. Previewing and rendering individual files never publish them by themselves.

title: Getting started
text:
7 First build checklist

Set both titles and author metadata, then list only existing chapters and decks.
Export the bibliography from Zotero into root assets/ and run the slide script to refresh its local copy.
Render one representative chapter and one deck, including their Python cells if present.
Check both book profiles and the notebook output before sharing them.
Commit the course sources and required local dependencies. Exclude generated output according to your repository policy.

Continue with the Book guide or Slide guide. For the underlying mechanisms, see Quarto projects and project profiles.

title: Slide guide
text:
Extension: clean 1.4.1 · Local customisation
slides/_quarto.yml loads slides/_template.yml. The shared file selects format: clean-revealjs, supplies plugin settings and references local resources. The clean extension lives under slides/_extensions/grantmcdermott/clean/; its clean.scss contains both upstream styling and local modifications.
The palette uses dark teal #23373b, teal #2F4647, orange #EB811B and a #fafafa slide background. Body text uses Roboto and headings Roboto Slab. The shared format enables a fast fade transition, simple callouts, hover code annotations, a chalkboard and the Font Awesome stylesheet.


The deck below was rendered with a local copy of the actual slide theme and extensions. Click inside it, then use the arrow keys. Open it separately for full-screen use.


Open the demonstration deck · Download its source

text:
Extension: clean 1.4.1 · Local customisation
slides/_quarto.yml loads slides/_template.yml. The shared file selects format: clean-revealjs, supplies plugin settings and references local resources. The clean extension lives under slides/_extensions/grantmcdermott/clean/; its clean.scss contains both upstream styling and local modifications.

title: Slide guide
text:
2 Headings, columns and content
Native layouts · Local helpers
Use ## for a normal content slide. A # heading introduces a higher-level section and can create a vertical stack, depending on the surrounding heading structure. Put speaker-only content inside .notes.
## A scientific comparison

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
Describe the prediction.
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](assets/example.png){width=100%}
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Ask students to identify the evidence before discussing the mechanism.
:::

2.1 Code beside its result
The theme includes .columns3070, .columns7030, .columns4060 and .columns6040. They set the widths of direct .column children; the first number is the first column’s percentage. They are particularly useful with Quarto’s code-output column layout:
```{python}
#| output-location: column
#| classes: columns4060
print("A result beside the code")
```
These classes are layout helpers, not standalone commands that generate columns. Use native .columns / .column markup or output-location: column to create the structure first.







Helper
Effect




.right
Applies text-align: right to the element’s content.


.small-gap
A block with 0.25em top and bottom margins; useful for small spacing adjustments.


.no-title on a slide heading
Hides h1, h2 and h3 descendants of that slide. It hides subheadings too, not just the slide title.


.etable wrapping an image
Fits table images within the available box using contained image dimensions.



## A descriptive source heading {.no-title}

![](assets/example.png){width=85%}
Keep source headings meaningful even when hidden. Menu, navigation and accessibility behaviour should be checked for the resulting deck.

title: Slide guide
text:
3 Text highlighting
Local theme rules
[Important phrase]{.bg}
[Main emphasis]{.alert}
[Alternative]{.alert-blue}
[Positive result]{.alert-green}
[Caution]{.alert-red}
[Another category]{.alert-purple}
[Custom colour]{.fg style="--col: #007b83"}







Class
Configured value




.bg
Orange gradient at approximately 40–50% opacity; wraps across lines.


.alert
Theme orange, #EB811B.


.alert-blue
#5858a1.


.alert-green
#67b06a.


.alert-red
#d7191c.


.alert-purple
#9a26b0.


.fg
CSS variable --col, falling back to #131516.



Bold text uses teal. Inline code also uses teal with a translucent background and a monospace font stack. .bg in the book uses teal instead of this slide orange; the source syntax is shared but the appearance is intentionally format-specific.
For a compact action link, the theme also supplies .button:
[Open the published course](https://example.org){.button}
It renders an orange button with a triangle prefix and a blue hover state. It is distinct from the book’s .btn-download style.

title: Slide guide
text:
4 Images, captions and video
Native media · Local positioning
![A caption explaining the evidence](assets/example.png){width=80% .img-up-25}







Class
Relative vertical offset




.img-up-0
0px


.img-up-25, .img-up-50, .img-up-75
-25px, -50px, -75px


.img-up-100, .img-up-150
-100px, -150px


.img-down-25, .img-down-50, .img-down-75
25px, 50px, 75px



Apply a class directly to the image or to a wrapper containing it. These offsets use position: relative: they shift the visible element while retaining its original layout space. They do not resize an image or reserve extra room for overlapping content. Use ordinary width/height controls first, then inspect the finished slide before adjusting an offset.
Quarto’s native automatic stretching primarily applies to non-nested images. Images inside columns, fragment wrappers or stacks often need explicit size controls. For image enlargement, add .lightbox and enable lightbox: true in the document or local project metadata. Existing course sources use .lightbox, but the central shared YAML does not currently enable lightbox globally.
The current theme sets figure captions to Roboto, centred, with a -15px relative top offset and a very small 0.07em font size. This is the implemented value, not a recommended readable caption size. Override it in course-specific CSS if captions must be legible in a lecture room; do not assume a standard Quarto caption size.
For a local video, use an HTML element when you need the theme’s r-stretch rule:
<video class="r-stretch" controls src="assets/process.mp4"></video>
The CSS constrains width to 100%, bounds the maximum height and centres the video. The theme also sets all slide-section padding to zero. Neither rule guarantees an oversized video fits every surrounding layout. Include the video file when extracting the slide project.

title: Slide guide
Slide guide
text:
6 Animation

6.1 Native auto-animation
Native Reveal.js
Use adjacent slides with auto-animate=true to animate matching elements. Explicit data-id values make the intended match clear:
## First position {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="concept" style="margin-left: 0;"}
A scientific concept
:::

## Second position {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="concept" style="margin-left: 120px;"}
A scientific concept
:::
This does not require the animate extension. The working demonstration includes a matching two-slide sequence.


6.2 SVG animation with the animate extension
Extension: fradav/animate 0.2.0
The template declares animate in both revealjs-plugins and filters. The filter recognises a code block whose first two classes are yaml and animate, then emits a data-animate container with the named SVG resource.
```{.yaml .animate src="assets/process.svg"}
setup:
  - element: "#particle"
    modifier: opacity
    parameters: [0]
animation:
  - element: "#particle"
    modifier: opacity
    parameters: [1]
    duration: 800
```
The SVG must contain an element with the matching ID. setup supplies initial SVG.js modifications; animation supplies subsequent changes. duration is expressed in milliseconds. Plugin autoplay defaults to true. Serve the deck with quarto preview or an HTTP server: this plugin fetches external SVG data, which can fail when opened directly with file://.
The extension folder contains its JavaScript dependencies. Transfer the filter declaration, plugin declaration, whole extension folder and SVG assets together. See the upstream animate reference for timelines and fragment-indexed sequences; native auto-animation and this SVG plugin are different systems.

title: Slide guide
text:
7 Navigation and repeated headings
Native controls · Extension: verticator · Local scripts
The clean theme enables slide numbers and configures the menu panel on the left. Local CSS moves the menu button to the top right, chalkboard buttons alongside it, a supplied logo to the bottom left and slide numbers to the bottom right. A logo is shown only if configured in the local document or project.
The shared verticator settings use themetag: h1, clickable: true, automatic placement, offset: 3vmin, title tooltips and scale: 0.75. Its section indicators are most useful with vertical stacks; they are not a replacement for the slide menu.
Use the arrow keys for slide navigation. Reveal’s help panel (?), overview (Esc) and speaker view (S) are native presentation tools. Speaker view can require a served page and browser popup permission. The chalkboard is enabled by shared metadata; browser annotations do not become editable annotations in an exported PDF.

7.1 Repeated slide titles
The active script is slides/assets/after-body.html, included by shared YAML. It groups real slide sections by the text of their first h1, h2 or h3 and rewrites repeated headings as Title (1/3), Title (2/3) and so on. Stack-container sections and sections with data-visibility="hidden" are excluded. Equal titles are grouped across the deck, even when not adjacent.
Do not add counters manually. The script changes heading text in the browser, so it is not an authoring-time numbering system and its results should be checked after rendering. A separate assets/js/same-title-counter.js file exists but is not included by the current shared configuration; do not load both.


7.2 Links in new tabs
The same after-body script gives links inside .reveal .slides target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer", except links with empty URLs, #... fragment links and links carrying .lightbox. This applies to relative course-page links as well as external URLs. It runs during initial setup and Reveal readiness; content added dynamically afterwards is not automatically reprocessed.

title: Slide guide
text:
8 Citations and mathematics
Native citations and MathJax · Local resources
The slide project’s bibliography points to slides/assets/your-course.bib, using bibliography: assets/your-course.bib in its local YAML. Shared YAML supplies the local CSL path. Use [@yourKey] or @yourKey in slide text and ::: {#refs} on a references slide. The local .csl-entry style uses Roboto at 14pt; long lists can still overflow.
The clean extension loads a MathJax 4 CDN script plus the slide-root mathjax-config.js. The local configuration requests the Asana font and \(...\) / \[...\] TeX delimiters for MathJax scanning. Quarto still accepts ordinary $...$ and $$...$$ authoring syntax. Keep the root slides/mathjax-config.js when copying the project; a similarly named extension resource also exists and is not a reason to omit that root file.

title: Slide guide
text:
9 Author profile icons
Local course/author-links filter
Configure personal details in slides/_quarto.yml:
author:
  - name: Sébastien Biass
    orcid: 0000-0002-1919-9473
author-links:
  researchgate: https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sebastien-Biass
  github: https://github.com/e5k
  scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Vs5kVHEAAAAJ
  website: https://e5k.github.io
The filter runs for Reveal.js when author-links is present. It accepts only values starting with http:// or https://; absent or nonmatching values are skipped. At least one valid profile URL is needed before it injects any additional icon behaviour.
It targets the first .quarto-title-author-name, inserting links after an existing ORCID icon or after the name when ORCID is absent. The order is ResearchGate, GitHub, Scholar, Website. It replaces the native ORCID graphic with a Font Awesome icon when present. It does not add a separate set of personal links for every author.
All five icons use #2F4647 at 55% opacity and full opacity on hover or keyboard focus. They receive accessible labels and open in a new tab. Shared YAML declares course/author-links; its implementation is slides/_extensions/course/author-links/author-links.lua with a companion _extension.yml. Font Awesome is provided by the shared CDN stylesheet. Keep URLs local when transferring the reusable filter.

title: Slide guide
text:
10 Extract a standalone slide project
Local portability convention

Refresh bibliography copies with python scripts/render_slides.py 2 --no-pdf from the course root. It copies all root assets/*.bib, replacing same-named slide copies, before rendering.
Check that image, data, CSL, code and style paths needed by the selected decks stay inside slides/. Course-specific data and plots.mplstyle are copied locally when needed; they are not fetched automatically.
Copy the entire slides/ directory, including _quarto.yml, _template.yml, _extensions/, assets/, mathjax-config.js and any data/ or img/ directories.
Activate an environment with the deck’s Python dependencies and run quarto preview inside the copied folder.

The book’s scripts are outside the extracted project, but direct Quarto commands work inside it. quarto preview does not refresh Zotero copies. For an independent talk, maintain its bibliography directly in its own assets/. Relative links to published course pages may still need adjustment when publishing at another address; distinguish those reading links from files required to build the deck.

title: Slide guide
text:
11 Export behaviour
render_slides.py exports PDFs through decktape reveal --fragments, so fragment states can produce additional PDF pages. This is different from a static one-page-per-source-slide export. --no-compress skips Ghostscript; --no-pdf skips PDF generation entirely. The shared pdf: true setting is not a replacement for the script’s Decktape step.
PDFs cannot retain interactive fragment controls, animation, hover effects, lightboxes or playable videos. Check layout and the sequence of captured fragment states separately. Browser-based mathematical rendering and dynamically fetched SVG animations may need extra time or network access during capture.
For native options beyond this template, see Reveal.js, advanced layouts and animation and presentation tools.
